comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Treatment of DVA and Materiality of Realized Gains
comparisons.peer_summary: Unrealized gains or losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) for elected liabilities are recorded in OCI, while realized gains or losses are recorded in principal transactions revenue. Realized gains or losses from instrument-specific credit risk were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase disclose that gains or losses related to their fair value option elections were not material for the fiscal year 2024. JPM specifically notes that realized gains/losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) recorded in principal transactions revenue were not material for 2024, 2023, and 2022, aligning with GS's statement that fair value changes on loans held for investment were not material in 2024 and 2023 and were included in other principal transactions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Reporting and Classification Details for Level 3 Instruments
comparisons.peer_summary: Level 3 derivatives are presented on a net basis. Realized and unrealized gains/losses on Level 3 AFS securities were not material for 2024-2022, with unrealized gains/losses due to DVA for fair value option elected liabilities reported in OCI as $(50) million, $(158) million, and $(529) million respectively. Other items include changes in fair value for MSRs in mortgage fees, DVA in principal transactions revenue, loan originations included in purchases, and maturities/repayments.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the materiality of fair value changes. JPM explicitly states in its Level 3 rollforward footnote that realized gains/losses due to DVA for fair value option elected liabilities reported in principal transactions revenue were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022. This mirrors GS's disclosure in Item 8 that gains/losses from changes in fair value of loans held for investment were not material for 2024 and 2023 and were included in other principal transactions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment of loans at fair value
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value within Trading assets, with changes recognized in earnings. This accounting treatment excludes these loans from the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies.
comparisons.comparison: While GS focuses on the materiality outcome (not material) of fair value changes on loans, Morgan Stanley defines the accounting treatment for such loans, stating that loans with the fair value option elected are carried at fair value with changes recognized in earnings. Unlike GS, which quantifies the lack of materiality for 2024, MS describes the mechanical recognition in earnings without specifying the materiality magnitude for the current year in this specific sentence, though it notes these loans are excluded from allowance for credit losses.
